requirements.description: Fellowships are provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility; excellence of the researcher is the core scope criterion for the fellowship.

European Postdoctoral Fellowships must take place in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe Associated Country and are open to researchers of any nationality who wish to engage in R&I projects by coming to Europe or moving within Europe.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships must include an outgoing phase of 12–24 months in a non-associated Third Country and a mandatory 12-month return phase to a host organisation in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country; restricted to European nationals or long-term residents.

Training activities implemented under Postdoctoral Fellowships must integrate key transferable skills and competences common to all fields, including digital skills (e.g. generative AI), and foster the culture of Open Science, knowledge valorisation, and when applicable innovation and entrepreneurship, as well as research integrity.

A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, covering research objectives, training and career needs, transferable skills training, teaching, publications, and public/citizen science engagement; must be submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action.

Fellowships must empower fellows to pursue research careers and prepare them for increased research collaboration and information-sharing through digital technologies (collaborative tools, Open Access, FAIR data management, societal engagement, citizen science).

Researchers may optionally include a secondment phase within the overall fellowship duration; for European Fellowships, secondments cannot exceed half the requested duration (excluding non-academic placement periods) and must add significant value and impact to the fellowship.

Proposals may optionally include an additional non-academic sector placement of up to six months at the end of the project; the request must be an integral part of the proposal with added-value explained, and is subject to evaluation; placement must be at an organisation established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

ERA Fellowships providing support for researchers undertaking their fellowship in a widening country may be applied for under Work Programme Annex 11 to help spread excellence and contribute to balanced brain circulation.

Proposals in Euratom research areas must meet specific eligibility conditions applicable to that programme area; Euratom fellowships are supported through an indicative annual EUR 1 million contribution from the Euratom Research and Training Programme.
